Respondents Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice
Rajesh Shankar

For the Petitioner : Mrs. Neetu Singh, ADvocate For the Respondents : Mr.
Ratnesh Kumar, S.C. (L&C)-I Order No. 08 Dated: 09.08.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the State respondents to pay adequate monetary compensation to the petitioner for using his land appertaining to plot nos. 553 and 558, Khata No. 445, Mouza- Chas, District- Bokaro by constructing government road (from Jamgoria to Chirachas) without issuance of any prior notice or obtaining his consent/no objection.
The petitioner has also made other related prayers.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner purchased the aforesaid land measuring area of 16.75 decimals vide registered sale deed no. 10113 dated 19.12.1980 from Shankar Kumar Mahto and others.
Subsequently out of the said land, the petitioner sold an area of 11 decimals to one Ram Vilas Paswan in the year 2006 and thereafter he remained in possession of 5.75 decimals of land.
The petitioner kept on paying rent to the government, in lieu of which the rent receipts were also issued to him till the year 2016-17.
His name was also being shown as raiyat in the revenue records of the government till 2019.

When the petitioner visited the said land in the Shankar Prasad Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... on 9 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85696123/
1 beginning of the year 2016, he was surprised to find that a PCC road was built by the government without his consent or paying any compensation to him.

entities.text: Shankar Prasad Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, he approached the Circle Officer, Chas (the respondent no. 6) and also filed a written application regarding measurement of the said land.
The respondent no. 6, vide letter dated 13.04.2016, directed the Circle Amin, Chas to measure the said land.
The measurement was accordingly done by the Circle Amin preparing a trace map and report was submitted to the respondent no. 6.

On the basis of the said report and trace map, the respondent no. 6, vide order dated 12.05.2017 passed in Land Measurement Record No.
01/2016-17, stated that a pucca road was constructed by the government over the petitioner's land.

The petitioner also filed an application under the Right to Information Act, 2005 in the office of the District Land Acquisition Officer, Bokaro seeking details of the acquisition as well as payment made to the raiyats in lieu thereof.
Subsequently, it was informed to him that no acquisition proceeding was initiated with respect to the said land.
The petitioner also raised his grievance in the portal of 'Mukhyamantri Jan Samwad Kendra', however the same was not redressed.
Hence, the present writ petition.

3. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 and 3 stating that a soil-gravel/metal road was already existing on the said part of land which was only upgraded by the Rural Development Department, Government of Jharkhand in the year 2013-14 under the State Welfare Planning.

entities.text: Rural Development Department, Government of Jharkhand
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said road was being used by the residents of the said area for last 45-50 years.

Though the part of the land is being shown as 'raiyati', yet no compensation was paid by the government to any person as the said road being used by the local residents was already upgraded in the year 1980.

The said upgradation work continued for about 09 months, however during the said period, the petitioner neither claimed his ownership nor made any correspondence with the department seeking any compensation.

In support of the said submission, a copy of letter no. 1735 dated 10.10.2019 issued by the Executive Engineer, Rual Development Department (Rural Works Affairs), Work Division, Bokaro to the respondent no. 6 has been annexed as Annexure-A to the counter affidavit.

entities.text: Rual Development Department (Rural Works Affairs), Work Division
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
5.
The petitioner has claimed that he purchased the land in question in the year 1980 by way of a registered sale deed.

After selling the part of the said land, he was in possession of 5.75 decimals of the same over which the Department of Rural Development, Government of Jharkhand has constructed a road without taking his consent or making payment of due compensation whereas the stand of the respondent nos. 2 and 3 taken in the counter affidavit is that the soil-gravel/metal road was existing on the said part of land for last 45-50 years and was being used by the local residents/villagers.

entities.text: Department of Rural Development, Government of Jharkhand
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The letter dated 1735 dated 10.10.2019 also suggests that in the year 1980 when the petitioner had purchased the said land, the government road was already existing.

The said road was also upgraded in the year 1980 and subsequently further upgradation was made in the year 2013-14 by the Rural Development Department and during the said work, the petitioner neither claimed his raiyati right over the same nor demanded any compensation.

Though the petitioner has claimed that he was shown as raiyat of the said land in revenue records till 2019 and rent receipts were also issued in his favour till 2016-17, yet the aforesaid facts stated in the counter affidavit have not been denied by him, particularly to the extent that the road, which was upgraded in the year Shankar Prasad Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... on 9 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85696123/
2 2013-14, was being used by the residents of the area for last 45-50 years and in the year 1980 also,
i.e., the year in which the petitioner purchased the said land, the same was being used by the general public.

entities.text: Shankar Prasad Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Under the aforesaid circumstance, this Court is not inclined to enter into the said factual aspects under extraordinary writ jurisdiction.
Accordingly, no writ of mandamus can be issued to the respondents as has been prayed by the petitioner in the present writ petition.
The same is accordingly dismissed.
7. The petitioner is, however, at liberty to take other/alternative recourse(s) available under law before a fact finding court/forum.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
